lane: Claude 2.1.311 adaptation — what blinds a managed session without a flag, re-verified

static.method: Read-only inspection of the digest-pinned executable. Each fact is bound to its anchor by digest and byte offset, and to an 8 KiB window around it by digest; no source text is retained. For 2.1.311 every 2.1.308 anchor was recovered from the promoted darwin-arm64 bytes by its digest, matched identifier-agnostically (minified names change every build) in the 2.1.311 linux-x64 artifact and in the 2.1.308 linux-x64 artifact (sha256 356733f185fa988e6bf3aa9a555269fdd167982a2e2a80d3c8a78037bb92ad58, the promoted bytes), and the code around it compared modulo minified names; each fact below re-read unchanged.

facts.fact: One parser reads every switch: off when unset or empty; otherwise on only when the value, lowercased and trimmed, is 1, true, yes or on. The env registry's bool() type is the same parser.
Simple (bare) mode is CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE read by that parser, or --bare in argv before `--`.
Safe mode is CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE read by that parser, or --safe-mode in argv before `--`.
CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED, read by that parser, stands for --restricted.
The customization gate: in bare mode the hooks surface is off (hooks: true in its skip table), so no settings, flag, policy or plugin hook fires; the status line is not in it.

The effective hooks: policy disableAllHooks → none; policy allowManagedHooksOnly, or safe mode → policy hooks only; policy strictPluginOnlyCustomization covering hooks → policy hooks only; the merged settings' disableAllHooks → policy hooks only; else the merged hooks of every enabled source.
Settings sources, low to high precedence: userSettings, projectSettings, localSettings, flagSettings (--settings), policySettings.
The enabled sources are the --setting-sources list plus flagSettings and policySettings, always.
--restricted or CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED empties the setting sources: the person's user, project and local layers are not read; flag and policy still are.
An HTTP hook reads allowedHttpHookUrls and httpHookAllowedEnvVars from the effective settings.
facts.note: The TLS-related environment names an HTTP hook passes through are now one shared list (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED moved into it); the gate is unchanged.

facts.fact: An HTTP hook whose URL matches no allowedHttpHookUrls pattern is blocked.
A header variable not in the hook's allowedEnvVars (narrowed by httpHookAllowedEnvVars) is not interpolated.
An allowedHttpHookUrls pattern is a URL with `*` wildcards; the port must match unless wildcarded, and `/*` matches any path.
CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is written, not read, on the local path: Claude exports its own session id when the variable is present (it only latches a cloud session reference otherwise).

Policy settings are read from managed-settings.json and managed-settings.d/*.json in the platform's admin directory (plus the Windows registry, WSL inheritance, remote and helper policy): not a file the adapter can read in full.
Hooks do not execute in a workspace whose trust dialog has not been accepted.
CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICT_PERSONAL_CONFIG (new in 2.1.308), read by the switch parser or set by a managed source, turns on restrict-personal-config mode.
In that mode a personal hook that fails on PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PreModelSwitch, UserPromptSubmit or UserPromptExpansion fails closed (blocks the action).
facts.note: 2.1.311 (Windows without Git Bash only): the "noBash" fail-closed rule no longer exempts command hooks that set shell "powershell", and a hook ending with exit code 127 gets its own message. The fail-closed event set is unchanged; the adapter sets no shell on its managed hooks.

facts.fact: CLAUDE_CODE_IGNORE_PERSISTED_TRUST (new in 2.1.308) makes no persisted workspace-trust record count in this process, so hooks wait for the trust dialog again (trust-gates-hooks).

The common hook input is built in one place: session_id, transcript_path ("" in a diskless session), cwd, scratchpad_dir (only when a scratchpad exists), prompt_id, permission_mode, agent_id, agent_type, effort.
A served (remote-caller) hook call carries session_id "served:<caller session>" and an empty transcript_path; it does not originate from a local terminal launch.

scan.method: The 2.1.308 scan carried forward name by name, re-checked against the 2.1.311 env registry; every adapter-referenced env name and settings key is still present. New registry names on these paths blind nothing: CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT_HOOK_EVENTS only adds UserPromptSubmit hook_started/hook_response messages to the SDK stream, and CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS (dangerous rm without a prompt in bypass mode) is withdrawn whenever a PermissionRequest hook is registered, as the adapter's are. The settings source labels add mcpMount ("Remote Control server mount"), a display label outside the five settings layers.

live.method: The isolated loopback rig of invocation-grammar.json, with managed settings in the adapter's own shape: SessionStart through the adapter's command forwarder, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SessionEnd as HTTP hooks whose Authorization header names $PUPPETEER_HOOK_TOKEN (allowedEnvVars), all to a loopback bridge that checks the bearer. The person's user settings hold a command hook of theirs and a status line of theirs, plus what each probe sets. No owner configuration is read or written. Each session sets the placeholder ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, and only that placeholder reached the loopback model (an equality check; no value read). On this hosted linux container the artifact can find a host credential outside the disposable environment (findings.md, 2.1.311); these sessions redirected only the model endpoint, so egress to the artifact's hard-coded account and OAuth endpoints was neither recorded nor blocked. Re-run with packages/surface/vendors/claude/census/switch-probes.mjs: each probe is one native TUI session in a disposable environment against the loopback model; whether a tool ran is read from the workspace. F01-F16 reproduce the 2.1.308 record exactly, and each reads identically on the 2.1.308 linux-x64 artifact (sha256 356733f185fa988e6bf3aa9a555269fdd167982a2e2a80d3c8a78037bb92ad58, the promoted bytes) in the same environment.
